extracted.intended_audience: journalists, business leaders, policymakers, researchers, and the general informed public
extracted.subtask_description: A corporate press release/report presenting the 2018 Edelman Trust Barometer survey results, methodology notes, and key findings about trust in institutions, demographics, and source credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust Index
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trust Index is an average of a country’s trust in the institutions of government, business, media and NGOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the headline metric (global and country values shown). Values are presented (e.g., Global 64 for 2018) and can be explored by country and demographic. 'Values based on average percent trust.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions measured
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust is measured for four institutions: government, business, media and NGOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These institution-level trust scores are the components used to compute the Trust Index and to show institution-by-institution trends and country comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed Public definition
rubrics_metrics.description: All informed public respondents met the following criteria: aged 25-64, college-educated; household income in the top quartile for their age in their country; read or watch business/news media at least several times a week; follow public policy issues in the news at least several times a week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicitly defined respondent segment used to report a distinct set of trust results separate from the mass population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass Population definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Mass population respondents are aged 18+ and represent the portion of the population that do not meet the criteria for the Informed Public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as the broader comparator sample for trust measures; ensures segmentation between general public and informed public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust level bands
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorical bands for interpreting trust scores and classifying countries or groups as trusters, neutral, or distrusters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Values basis / measurement unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Values based on percent trust (and values based on average percent trust).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that reported figures represent percentages or averages of percent-trust responses rather than raw counts or other scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media definition and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents hold a broad definition of 'media' that can include platforms and search engines as well as journalism: social media (48 percent), search engines (25 percent), alongside journalism (89 percent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that confusion about what constitutes 'media' is linked to changes in overall media trust; the composition matters when interpreting media trust scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concern about fake news / perceived difficulty identifying trusted news
rubrics_metrics.description: Globally, nearly seven in 10 respondents among the general population worry about fake news or false information being used as a weapon, and 59 percent say that it is getting harder to tell if a piece of news was produced by a respected media organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items measure public anxiety about misinformation and perceived ability to judge news credibility; they contextualize declines in media trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source credibility by actor type
rubrics_metrics.description: Credibility ratings for different spokesperson types: journalists have risen 12 points; CEOs recorded a seven-percentage point gain; technical experts, financial industry analysts, and successful entrepreneurs now register credibility levels of 50 percent or higher; 'a person like yourself' dipped to an all-time low.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracks which types of sources the public finds credible (or not) and how those perceptions shifted year-over-year; useful for evaluating spokesperson strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country-level polarization and change
rubrics_metrics.description: The world is moving apart in trust with a distinct split between extreme trust gainers and losers; example: United States had a 37-point aggregate drop in trust across all institutions, while China experienced a 27-point gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes large cross-country shifts and polarization; measures include aggregate changes across the four institutions and allow ranking of countries over time (Country Ranking, 2016-2018).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic breakdowns available
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust can be explored by institution, gender, age, and audience (Informed Public vs Mass Population).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that results are disaggregated across multiple demographic dimensions for more granular analysis and comparisons.
